description: Re-state the router's budget claims honestly — the ground moved under one of them. agora's record (docs/spike-litellm-leaf.md N4, docs/router-hand-built-behaviours.md, docs/prior-art.md) rests on the finding that LiteLLM's budget primitives are cumulative and merely ABORT, with no caller-supplied per-request ceiling that refuses a rung BEFORE dialing it. **That is no longer true as a category claim: LiteLLM now ships dollar-denominated pre-call budgets with `fail_closed_budget_enforcement`.** A hard budget ceiling is therefore no longer a differentiator, and any doc that still sells it as one is selling a stale comparison — the exact failure this repo's anti-fabrication discipline exists to prevent. What DOES remain ours, and is worth stating precisely because it is narrower and true: (1) the **`unpriced`-never-passes-a-ceiling rule** — LiteLLM's `cost_per_token` returns `(0, 0)` for an unmapped model, i.e. FREE where it means UNKNOWN, which is fail-OPEN on exactly the case a budget exists to catch; agora treats unpriced as un-ceilable and refuses; (2) **`budget_units` denomination** — the ceiling is expressed in the caller's own unit rather than assuming USD, which is what lets a non-currency budget (a quota, a credit, a research allocation) be enforced at all; (3) **non-text `measure()`** — a ceiling that means something for images, speech, music and video, not just tokens; and (4) the **always-completes terminal rung** — no surveyed gateway has one, and it is the invariant the whole supervision tree is built around: a fallback chain that terminates because its last entry CANNOT fail is a different guarantee from a chain that happens to have a last entry. Scope: docs and the roadmap. NO behaviour change — every claim restated here is already asserted by an existing test (tests/test_cost.py, tests/test_budget.py, tests/test_zero_spend.py and their Erlang counterparts), and the point of this tasklist is that the PROSE should say only what those tests prove. Where a doc's dated comparison is now stale, re-date it rather than deleting it: a superseded finding with its date attached is evidence; an undated one is a liability.

userStories.title: Retire the hard-budget-ceiling claim as a differentiator
userStories.description: Update every doc that presents a pre-dial budget ceiling as something only agora has. The comparison was true when it was measured and is not true now.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/prior-art.md and docs/router-hand-built-behaviours.md no longer present a hard/pre-call budget ceiling as an agora differentiator, and state the reason: LiteLLM ships dollar-denominated pre-call budgets with `fail_closed_budget_enforcement`.

docs/spike-litellm-leaf.md's N4 finding is RE-DATED rather than deleted — it stays as the evidence it was, with an explicit 'superseded as of 2026-08' note naming what changed, so the record shows a claim that was tested and later overtaken rather than a claim that was wrong.

No test, constant, or behaviour changes: the ceiling still refuses before the rung is dialed, and `tests/test_budget.py::TestTheCeilingStillRefuses` and its Erlang counterpart stay green — what changed is the marketing, not the mechanism.
Nothing anywhere in docs/ still implies agora is alone in enforcing budgets.

userStories.title: State the four claims that survive, each tied to the test that proves it
userStories.description: Replace the retired claim with the narrower true ones. Each must name its assertion, so a future survey can re-check it the same way this one was.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/prior-art.md states the `unpriced`-never-passes-a-ceiling rule with the specific contrast that makes it matter: LiteLLM's `cost_per_token` returns `(0, 0)` for an unmapped model — FREE where it means UNKNOWN, i.e. fail-OPEN on exactly the case a ceiling exists to catch — where agora treats unpriced as un-ceilable and refuses.

It states `budget_units` denomination (the ceiling is in the caller's own unit, not an assumed currency, which is what makes a non-currency quota enforceable) and non-text `measure()` (a ceiling that means something for image, speech, music, and video, not only tokens).

It states the always-completes terminal rung as the strongest surviving claim — no surveyed gateway has one — and articulates the distinction: a fallback chain that terminates because its last entry CANNOT fail is a different guarantee from a chain that merely has a last entry.

Each of the four claims names the assertion that holds it (tests/test_cost.py, tests/test_budget.py, tests/test_zero_spend.py and their Erlang counterparts), so every claim in the docs is checkable from the docs.

userStories.title: Date the comparisons and make re-checking them routine
userStories.description: The defect this tasklist fixes is not that a claim was wrong — it is that a dated competitive comparison was left undated and became prose. Prevent the recurrence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every competitive claim in docs/prior-art.md, docs/spike-litellm-leaf.md, and docs/router-hand-built-behaviours.md carries the date it was verified, so a reader can tell a fresh finding from a stale one without re-running the spike.

ROADMAP.md's Ongoing block gains a standing item: re-verify the router's competitive claims on a stated cadence, and re-date or retire each one — paired with, and cross-referenced to, the contract-version tracking item already there.
The roadmap and README carry no surviving claim that this tasklist retired from the docs.
No source file outside docs/ and ROADMAP.md is modified by this tasklist.
